comparisons.rationale: The synthetic numerator is forced by one bounded scenario path per policy and has no policy-year exposure denominator. The SOA/LIMRA value is derived from rounded totals across complete study years, uses exposure methodology, combines surrender and forfeiture, and reflects duration and product effects absent here.

reference_value.status: derived from approximate rounded headline totals

comparisons.rationale: The generator chooses two fictional labels randomly at issuance; they do not encode the source study's plan definitions. The source measure is multi-year exposure, while the synthetic measure is an issuance count in a 100-policy engineering fixture.
The methodological reference supports exposure-aware rate design and warns about partial-year errors. It supports the decision not to annualize current simulator proportions but supplies no target.

billing_frequency.definition: Issued policies grouped by fictional billing frequency.

grace_entry.definition: Policies with a transition to grace_period / generated policies.
grace_entry.unit: policy proportion over one generated scenario path

grace_recovery.definition: Policies returning to active / policies entering grace_period.
grace_recovery.unit: conditional policy proportion over one generated scenario path

payment_events.definition: Structured payment events; a recovery can create a second attempt.

premium_amount_cents.unit: integer USD cents; premium mode is not annualized

product_variant.definition: Issued policies grouped by fictional product variant.

scenario_mix.definition: Policies classified from complete structured histories / generated policies.
scenario_mix.unit: policy proportion over one generated scenario path

service_contact.definition: Policies with at least one structured service contact / generated policies.
service_contact.unit: policy proportion over one generated scenario path

terminal_outcomes.definition: Policies with a generated lapse or surrender outcome / generated policies.
terminal_outcomes.unit: policy proportion over one generated scenario path; not annualized

timing_days.definition: Whole-day effective-time intervals imposed by current scenario logic.

sources.definition_note: The report uses lapse to include terminations with value (surrenders) and without value (forfeitures).
sources.exposure_basis: Policy exposure calculated with the Balducci approach; the report also discusses face-amount exposure.
sources.limitations: Detailed segmented results are outside the public report; source experience is exposure-based and duration-sensitive.
sources.organization: Society of Actuaries Research Institute and LIMRA
sources.population: Fully underwritten single-life term and whole-life policies sold in the United States and its territories; 28 contributing companies.

published_totals.derived_value_warning: Computed from rounded headline totals; not presented by the source as an official aggregate lapse rate.

sources.study_period: Seven complete study years, 2016-2022, spanning policy anniversaries in 2015-2022.
sources.title: 2015-2022 Term and Whole Life Insurance Policy Surrender/Lapse Experience Study Report

sources.definition_note: Used to support the decision not to annualize one-cycle simulator proportions, not as a numerical calibration target.
sources.exposure_basis: Explains experience-rate calculations and warns about errors from combining partial rate years.

sources.population: Methodological educational material; no portfolio population.
